neet_phy_u07_t07_1.working: Surface tension is force per length (N/m). This equals energy per area: J/m^2 = N·m/m^2 = N/m.

neet_phy_u07_t07_2.working: A soap film has two surfaces, so W = 2TΔA = 2 × 0.03 × (30 × 10^-4 m^2) = 1.8 × 10^-4 J.

neet_phy_u07_t07_3.working: The film pulls on the wire along both surfaces, so F = 2TL = 2 × 0.04 × 0.05 = 4.0 × 10^-3 N.

neet_phy_u07_t07_4.working: Pure water on clean glass has contact angle about 0° (IV). Mercury on glass is about 140° (II). Detergent lowers both surface tension and contact angle (III). NaCl, being highly soluble, raises surface tension (I).

neet_phy_u07_t07_5.working: A is false: surface tension does not depend on area. B, C and D are true. E is false: when cohesion exceeds adhesion, the contact angle is obtuse.
